# Scene ablation pilot: historical evidence synthesis

## Scope and citation key

This audit covers batch 1 of 1, all 24 supplied student-trajectory files, S0065–S0088. Their model-reviewed chunk reports are the evidence base; raw image pixels and independent scene inspection are not supplied. Individual reports sometimes describe only their own chunk; the synthesis combines the supplied chunks without treating repeated histories or copies as independent trials. File counts are not counts of independent experiments.

All original paths share this prefix:
`/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/`.
In the matrix, each suffix below that prefix ends in `/trajectory.jsonl`; line numbers refer to that original JSONL file.

## Evidence matrix

## Comparison and interpretation

**Success, failure and partial progress.** Successful execution means the runner reported a saved render, sometimes `usable_render`, and possibly a selection; it does not establish a successful reconstruction. S0066, for example, executed three nonempty builds and selected the last, but its claimed framing and pose improvements were not independently inspected (lines 10–25). S0078 is a counterexample to assuming the final executed build was accepted: the student explicitly selected step 2 after step 3 had rendered, with no visible explanation (lines 17–22).

Timeout recovery is operational progress, not proof of a visual pass. S0074, S0075, S0079 and S0082–S0084 each show an initial no-image timeout followed by a changed program and successful rendering. The changes often combined geometry simplification, materials, sampling or requested engine changes, so the bottleneck and the contribution of any one change remain unknown. Conversely, S0087 preserved a successful step 2 when step 3 timed out (lines 11–18). S0067 and S0068 reached a render but were interrupted during subsequent review; neither supports a completed final-quality judgment. These are partial *workflow* outcomes, not established partial visual correctness.

S0065 and S0076 stopped at the model CLI boundary with exit 1 and no visible program; the named stderr logs are unavailable. They are not empty patches or demonstrated reconstruction-algorithm failures. No permission or branch stop is evidenced in this group. Nor does a renderer log saying zero changed files establish an empty patch: S0083 line 16 is an execution log, while its surrounding trajectory contains substantive programs. Student-reported wall-only or pale views in S0085 and S0077 are possible algorithmic or scene-behavior problems despite successful rendering, but their causes and repairs are not independently verified (S0085 lines 13–18; S0077 lines 13–17).

**Advice and agency.** No separately identified teacher message, teacher detection, diagnosis or proposed teacher update is evidenced in these student trajectories; directory labels do not establish one. Thus teacher-advice availability, actual receipt, adoption, execution and validation cannot be inferred. This is not a claim about unseen teacher-side records. In contrast, controller/user input is visible: S0066 and S0068 actually received pre-execution source-audit checklists and subsequently executed programs with corresponding dimension/key guards and World initialization (S0066 lines 4–9; S0068 lines 4–8). These checklists were not visual diagnoses. Generic runner review and timeout-repair prompts were also received; students then authored revisions, such as S0073’s camera and later appearance changes (lines 7–17). Image paths staged for a session show availability, not necessarily completed inspection: S0068’s review timed out without a response (lines 10–13).

**Transferable constraints versus scene-specific hypotheses.** The common single-image, editable-mesh workflow and, in the no-probes condition, prohibition of diagnostic probes constrain what can be observed. Source assertions, unique keys, material isolation and grouped transforms are evidenced construction safeguards, not proofs of physical contact or editability under every later operation. Code describes multiple objects, poses, colors and sometimes procedural textures, cameras and lights; names, parenting and coordinates do not independently verify visibility, support, connections, pose, texture fidelity, framing or illumination.

Student observations and causal explanations must remain distinct. S0066’s wide/high-camera hypothesis accompanied simultaneous camera, monitor and lamp changes (lines 10–14); S0071 changed camera and chaise pose together (lines 12–15). Their effects cannot be isolated. S0073’s successive camera and appearance families are a more separated comparison, although visual improvement remains unknown (lines 9–17). Particular workbench, kitchen, chaise and ship-compartment inventories and camera settings are student interpretations of particular unseen references, not transferable facts.

## Coverage and limits

The supplied reports cover all 24 inventoried files and their stated chunks in this one group and batch. Repeated prompts and embedded histories are not additional trials. The audit does not see the reference or rendered pixels, independent geometric tests, or formal visual scores; missing scores are unknown, not zero. Selection, `DONE`, render completion and student self-assessment are not independent acceptance or quality evidence. Old model cost cannot be recovered from its absence. The record supports no causal superiority claim among ablation labels.
